portInfo.description: Lučka uprava Split manages Croatia’s major passenger port. The City Port Basin handles passenger traffic, cruise ships and catamarans. Cruise technical pages publish berth and ship-size figures that differ between the English technical-data page (250 m length, 8.2 m draft, 10 berths, centre 200 m walk) and the Croatian cruising page (345 m length, 10.5 m draft, berths 150–265 m). SeaDays keeps both. Cruise traffic has grown since first calls in 2002 per the authority narrative.

gettingThere.fromTerminal: Port of Split — City Port Basin (cruise) — Gat sv. Duje 1, 21000 Split, Croatia
gettingThere.distanceToCity: Diocletian’s Palace / old town. Authority: city centre 200 m walking. Allow 5–15 min estimate; not independently surveyed. Railway station. 100 m walking per same page. Airport. 20 km on technical page (port overview also states 24 km — both noted).
gettingThere.publicTransport: Confirm local transport options with the ship on your call date.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Ask which City Port berth you are on — ferry traffic shares the basin.
